deep.reconstruction:
The page is a fragment, drawn sideways, written just before the systematic definitions on p.70 ('Groupoïdes de Teichmüller'). It sets up a commutative square of groupoids.

The square:
- Top row: C^±_dep ↪(imm) C̃^±_dep. Bottom row: C_dep ↪(imm) C̃_dep.
- The vertical arrows run from the bottom (oriented) row to the top (± or 'biorienté') row. They are labelled 'fid. ess. surj.' (fidèle, essentiellement surjectif).
- Each ±-groupoid has a structure functor to [±1], the one-object groupoid of the group {±1}. This is the signature (orientation character) of a homeomorphism.

Comparison with p.70 fixes the meaning:
- C_dep plays the role of the oriented topological Teichmüller groupoid (T_top or ST_top). Objects are compact oriented surfaces with boundary, possibly with a finite set S of marked boundary points. Morphisms are isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms.
- C^±_dep has the same objects but all isotopy classes of homeomorphisms as morphisms. ε: C^± → [±1] is the signature, and C is the fibre over +1.
- The inclusion C → C^± is therefore faithful and bijective on objects, hence essentially surjective. It is not full.
- The horizontal 'imm' arrows are the inclusions of the subgroupoids with Σ = ∅ into the 'divisé' versions (X, Σ, S), where Σ is a compact 1-submanifold of the interior. P.70 calls these 'sous-groupoïde ouvert', which matches 'immersion (ouverte)'.

The line '0 ~ π0(C_dep) ≅ π0(C^±_dep) ≅ …' is unfinished. It records that passing to orientation-free morphisms does not change isomorphism classes. Every compact surface (with marked boundary points, or with a dividing 1-submanifold) admits an orientation-reversing self-homeomorphism, for example a reflection. So two objects isomorphic by some homeomorphism are already isomorphic by an orientation-preserving one. The trailing '≅' presumably continues to the set of combinatorial/topological types (genus, number of boundary components, marked-point data).

The drawings:
- The faint contour drawing continues p.68. There, a graph with vertices labelled 0, 1, ∞ (a dessin / bicoloured map with face centres) is surrounded by nested level curves. These look like the level lines of a height or modulus function, e.g. |f| for a Belyi-type map, or a Morse/Strebel-type exhaustion, with small circles marking critical points or holes.
- The small pencil sketch is a polygon (one side curved) starred from an interior vertex into triangles. This is the typical local picture of a cell in a triangulation or barycentric subdivision attached to a map or a pants-type decomposition.

The page serves the 1983 programme of the Teichmüller tower (groupoids of surfaces with boundary and their 'divided' versions). It prepares the formal definitions on the next page.
errors: The claimed bijection π0(C_dep) → π0(C^±_dep) is correct for purely topological surface data. It would fail for chiral combinatorial objects (e.g. chiral maps/dessins), so it depends on the objects being topological, as on p.70. No genuine error on the page.
The diagram is incomplete: the '0 ~' line and the final '≅' are unfinished.

ideas.what: Oriented vs. 'biorienté' Teichmüller groupoids, related by a faithful, essentially surjective functor. The ± version fibres over the groupoid [±1] via the orientation character, with the oriented one as fibre.
ideas.modern_name: Extended mapping class groupoid / extension 1 → Mod⁺ → Mod^± → Z/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Dehn, Nielsen, Baer); groupoid formulation in Grothendieck's Esquisse and later Teichmüller-tower literature (Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Moore–Seiberg)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Teichmüller tower discussion, which also mentions complex conjugation/orientation reversal

ideas.what: Open immersion of the undivided groupoid into the 'divisé' groupoid (surfaces with a dividing 1-submanifold Σ)
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid of surfaces with curve systems / decompositions (pants decomposition groupoid)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); Hatcher–Thurston, Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov for the decomposition complex
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in the Esquisse; the specific 'TD' notation is in these notes

ideas.what: π0 invariance under adding orientation-reversing morphisms, using the existence of orientation-reversing self-homeomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Classification of surfaces up to homeomorphism equals classification up to oriented homeomorphism
Level sets of |f| for a Belyi map; Strebel/ribbon-graph description of a dessin
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (dessins d'enfants); Strebel, Penner, Kontsevich for ribbon graphs

deep.surprise_reason: This is a formal set-up fragment: an oriented vs. unoriented mapping class groupoid with its signature functor, and an inclusion into 'divided' surfaces. It is standard and also visible in the Esquisse. The drawings are illustrative and unannotated. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The vertical arrows go from the oriented (lower) groupoids up to the ± groupoids, labelled 'fid. ess. surj.' (fidèle essentiellement surjectif). The upward arrows to '[±1]' are the signature functors.
The right-hand objects read as something like '𝒮C̃^±_dep' and 'C̃_dep' (tilde/divided versions). The '[?]' markers can be replaced by these.
The bottom line is '0 ~ π₀(C_dep) ⥲ π₀(C^±_dep) ≃' (unfinished).
